ARIMA(1,1,1) forecast of a count series

Source: R/tsd.R
arimfc.Rd

Fits ARIMA(1,1,1) to a series of counts (monthly incidents, calls for service, admissions) by exact maximum likelihood, the Kalman filter on the state-space form with the conditional-sum-of-squares fit as its start, as stats::arima() does by default, and forecasts h periods ahead with their standard errors. AIC is \(-2 \log L + 2(k + 1)\); BIC is \(\mathrm{AIC} + (k + 1)(\log n - 2)\), \(k\) the ARMA coefficients.

Usage

arimfc(y, h = 12)

Arguments

y

The counts, in time order, 24 at least.

h

The periods to forecast, at most 67108864 (2^26).

Value

A list of class arimfc: fc and se (forecasts and their standard errors), coef (ar1, ma1), sigma2, aic, bic and n.

References

Box, G. E. P. and Jenkins, G. M. (1970). Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control. Holden-Day.

Gardner, G., Harvey, A. C. and Phillips, G. D. A. (1980). Algorithm AS 154: an algorithm for exact maximum likelihood estimation of autoregressive-moving average models by means of Kalman filtering. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society C, 29(3), 311-322.

See also

Other counts over time: catcor(), fpdens(), lvfit(), ousim(), sarfc()

Examples

# 48 simulated months of counts
set.seed(1)
y <- rpois(48, 50 + 10 * sin(1:48 / 6))
arimfc(y, h = 6)$fc
#> [1] 61.03613 61.69301 61.79991 61.81731 61.82014 61.82060
